why: Hallgerd Ljotsson is the noble lady of Noble Houses; a hook about a customer paying her fits a shopkeeper, not her
Refr Styrkarsson is master of granaries; an apprentice taking 'the recipes' fits a craftsman, not a granary office
Lofn Helgason is the prison warden, not a magistrate; 'an old ruling of theirs' taking a widow's house misfits her office
Leidolf Illugason is the smuggling network's head in PEOPLE; 'Spymaster' is the Underground network's kind of title, not his
'The trade runs high' in furs; LAND gives Furs & Pelts impaired, hunting grounds depleted, no fur import; tanner is marked short of hides
'told by Deception' prints a capitalised skill key as prose
heading says 3 impaired but twelve rows under it are marked short (barrels, carving, charcoal, leather, lumber, boots, ore) with no impaired chip
crier proclaims 'royal decrees'; GOVERNMENT is a Grand Merchant Oligarchy with no crown or monarch among its powers
'Little cloth is made here' vs bolts of cloth drying across the yards; TRADE imports wool and exports fine textiles; weavers unmarked
rival crews fighting for the streets, people paying cut and brawling; page also says little crime, nothing happens to people; safety Very Safe
'the garrison and city watch sees to that': compound subject with singular verb
secret has the collier burning and selling charcoal from others' woods; page and LAND gaps say no timber reaches the charcoal burner
carpenter sells surplus wood on the side; the page marks the carpenters short of timber, timber needed and not brought in

cooper filled a large order of oak casks; the page marks the cooper 'Short of timber', barrel making short
'How they deal Short of grapes.' the shortage mark is set in front of the dealing line, followed by talk of the year's grapes
sawyer talks of which timber is good this year and who buys it; page says no timber reaches the sawmill, marked short
auctioneer's temperament 'incorruptible' beside his own secret of planting bidders to drive up prices
tie labelled 'inseparable', yet the two in-laws 'avoid each other everywhere else'
